tools.name: archive_camera_clip
tools.description: Moves a recorded clip from a camera's live recordings folder into the long-term archive folder for that camera. The clip is no longer in the live recordings folder after the move.

params.name: camera_id
params.description: Identifier of the camera that recorded the clip, e.g. 'front-door-cam'.

params.name: clip_filename
params.description: File name of the clip in the camera's recordings folder, e.g. '2026-10-04T18-22-10.mp4'.

tools.name: send_homeowner_device_alert
tools.description: Sends a push notification about a device event (e.g. leak detected, door left unlocked, smoke alarm) to the homeowner's phones through the Pushover service.

params.name: device_name
params.description: Friendly name of the device raising the alert, e.g. 'Basement Leak Sensor'.

params.name: event
params.description: Short description of what happened, e.g. 'Water detected'.

params.name: severity
params.description: One of 'info', 'warning', or 'critical'. Critical alerts bypass quiet hours and repeat until acknowledged.

params.name: room
params.description: Room where the device is installed, included in the message if given.

tools.name: purchase_replacement_part
tools.description: Charges the household's saved card for a replacement part or consumable for a smart home device, such as a thermostat air filter or smart lock battery pack.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Stripe customer ID of the household account.

params.name: payment_method_id
params.description: Saved Stripe payment method ID to charge.

params.name: part_sku
params.description: SKU of the replacement part, e.g. 'FLT-20x25-MERV11'.

tools.code:
import os

import stripe
from agents import function_tool

stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"]


@function_tool
def purchase_replacement_part(
    customer_id: str,
    payment_method_id: str,
    part_sku: str,
    unit_price_cents: int,
    quantity: int = 1,
) -> dict:
    qty = max(1, min(int(quantity), 20))
    amount = int(unit_price_cents) * qty
    intent = stripe.PaymentIntent.create(
        amount=amount,
        currency="usd",
        customer=customer_id,
        payment_method=payment_method_id,
        off_session=True,
        confirm=True,
        description=f"Replacement part {part_sku} x{qty}",
        metadata={"part_sku": part_sku, "quantity": str(qty), "source": "home-agent"},
        idempotency_key=f"part-{customer_id}-{part_sku}-{qty}-{amount}",
    )
    return {
        "payment_intent_id": intent.id,
        "status": intent.status,
        "amount_cents": intent.amount,
        "part_sku": part_sku,
        "quantity": qty,
    }

tools.name: email_offline_devices_report
tools.description: Emails a report listing smart home devices that have gone offline to the given recipient, such as the homeowner or their installer, over the household's SMTP account.

params.name: recipient
params.description: Email address to send the report to.

params.name: devices
params.description: List of offline devices, each an object with 'name', 'room', and 'last_seen' fields.

params.name: home_name
params.description: Name of the home shown in the subject line, e.g. 'Lake House'.

tools.code:
import os import smtplib from email.message import EmailMessage from email.utils import formatdate, make_msgid from langchain_core.tools import tool SMTP_HOST = os.environ.get("HOMEHUB_SMTP_HOST", "smtp.gmail.com") SMTP_PORT = int(os.environ.get("HOMEHUB_SMTP_PORT", "587")) SMTP_USER = os.environ.get("HOMEHUB_SMTP_USER", "") SMTP_PASS = os.environ.get("HOMEHUB_SMTP_PASSWORD", "") SENDER = os.environ.get("HOMEHUB_SENDER", "Home Hub ") def _format_rows(devices: list) -> tuple[str, str]: text_lines = [] html_rows = [] for d in devices: name = str(d.get("name", "Unknown device")) room = str(d.get("room", "-")) seen = str(d.get("last_seen", "unknown")) text_lines.append(f"- {name} ({room}), last seen {seen}") html_rows.append(f"{name}{room}{seen}") html = ( "" + "".join(html_rows) + "
DeviceRoomLast seen
" ) return "\n".join(text_lines), html @tool def email_offline_devices_report(recipient: str, devices: list, home_name: str = "Home") -> dict: """Email a report of offline smart home devices to a recipient.""" if "@" not in recipient: return {"sent": False, "error": "Invalid recipient address."} if not devices: return {"sent": False, "error": "No offline devices to report."} text_body, html_table = _format_rows(devices) msg = EmailMessage() msg["Subject"] = f"[{home_name}] {len(devices)} device(s) offline" msg["From"] = SENDER msg["To"] = recipient msg["Date"] = formatdate(localtime=True) msg["Message-ID"] = make_msgid(domain="homehub.local") msg.set_content(f"The following devices at {home_name} are offline:\n\n{text_body}\n") msg.add_alternative( f"

The following devices at {home_name} are offline:

{html_table}", subtype="html", ) try: with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, timeout=20) as smtp: smtp.starttls() if SMTP_USER: smtp.login(SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS) smtp.send_message(msg) except (smtplib.SMTPException, OSError) as e: return {"sent": False, "error": str(e)} return {"sent": True, "recipient": recipient, "device_count": len(devices), "message_id": msg["Message-ID"]}
